en indvandrer.explanation: "En indvandrer" means "an immigrant". It comes from the verb "at indvandre" (to immigrate): "Han indvandrede i 2010" (He immigrated in 2010).

en indånding.explanation: "En indånding" means "an inhalation / breath". It is built from "ind" (in) and "at ånde" (to breathe). To say you take a deep breath, use "dyb" (deep): "en dyb indånding" (a deep breath).

en infektion.explanation: "En infektion" means "an infection". To say where the infection is, put the body part before it: "en halsinfektion" (a throat infection). To say you caught one, use "at få" (to get): "Han har fået en infektion" (He has got an infection).

en influencer.explanation: "En influencer" means "an influencer". To say you follow one online, use "at følge" (to follow): "Jeg følger en influencer på Instagram" (I follow an influencer on Instagram).

en ingeniør.explanation: "En ingeniør" means "an engineer". To name the kind of engineer, put a word in front: "maskiningeniør" (mechanical engineer).

en ingrediens.explanation: "En ingrediens" means "an ingredient". To ask what a recipe needs, use the plural: "Hvilke ingredienser skal jeg bruge?" (Which ingredients do I need?) To name the list on a package, say "en ingrediensliste" (an ingredient list).

en innovation.explanation: "En innovation" means "an innovation". Do not mix it up with "en opfindelse" (an invention), a thing someone makes for the first time: "Telefonen er en vigtig opfindelse" (The telephone is an important invention).

en inspektør.explanation: "En inspektør" means "an inspector". To name the kind of inspector, put a word in front: "en fødevareinspektør" (a food inspector).

en inspiration.explanation: "En inspiration" means "an inspiration". To say you get ideas from somewhere, use "at hente" (to fetch): "Vi henter inspiration fra Italien" (We get inspiration from Italy).

en installation.explanation: "En installation" means "an installation". To say how long it takes to put in a program, say: "Installationen tager to minutter" (The installation takes two minutes). In art it means a work built in a room: "Kunstneren har bygget en installation i museet" (The artist has built an installation in the museum).

en institution.explanation: "En institution" means "an institution". In Denmark it is also the word for a daycare for children, such as "en vuggestue" (a nursery) or "en børnehave" (a kindergarten). To say a child goes there, say: "Vores søn er i institution" (Our son is in daycare).

en instruks.explanation: "En instruks" means "an instruction". To say someone did what the rules told them, say: "Han handlede efter instruks" (He acted according to instructions).

en instruktion.explanation: "En instruktion" means "an instruction". To tell someone to read the steps, use the plural: "Læs instruktionerne først" (Read the instructions first). Do not mix it up with "en instruktør" (a director): "Instruktøren leder filmen" (The director leads the film).

en instruktør.explanation: "En instruktør" means "a director". To say who leads a film, say: "Instruktøren leder filmen" (The director leads the film). To name a sports teacher, put the sport in front: "en svømmeinstruktør" (a swimming instructor). Do not mix it up with "en direktør" (a company director): "Direktøren leder firmaet" (The company director runs the firm).

en integration.explanation: "En integration" means "integration". To talk about newcomers becoming part of society, say: "integration af flygtninge" (integration of refugees). To talk about computer systems, say: "integration mellem to systemer" (integration between two systems).

en interesse.explanation: "En interesse" means "an interest". To name the subject of your interest, add "for" (in): "Han har stor interesse for biler" (He has a big interest in cars). To say you are interested, use "at være interesseret i" (to be interested in): "Jeg er interesseret i historie" (I am interested in history).

en internetforbindelse.explanation: "En internetforbindelse" means "an internet connection". It is built from "internet" and "en forbindelse" (a connection). To say you have no signal, say: "Jeg har ingen forbindelse" (I have no connection).

en invasion.explanation: "En invasion" means "an invasion". It comes from the verb "at invadere" (to invade). To say a crowd of tourists fills a place, say: "en invasion af turister" (an invasion of tourists).

en investering.explanation: "En investering" means "an investment". To say what you invest in, add "i" (in): "en investering i uddannelse" (an investment in education). To say something is worth the money, say: "Den nye cykel er en god investering" (The new bike is a good investment).

en invitation.explanation: "En invitation" means "an invitation". It comes from the verb "at invitere" (to invite). To say you accept, use "at takke ja" (to say yes, thanks): "Jeg takker ja til invitationen" (I accept the invitation).

en irritation.explanation: "En irritation" means "an irritation". It comes from the verb "at irritere" (to irritate). To say your skin is irritated, say: "en irritation i huden" (an irritation in the skin).

en isbjørn.explanation: "En isbjørn" means "a polar bear". It is built from "is" (ice) and "en bjørn" (a bear). "Is" also means "ice cream", as in "Jeg vil have en is" (I want an ice cream).

en isbod.explanation: "En isbod" means "an ice cream stand". It is built from "is" (ice cream) and "en bod" (a small stall). "Is" also means "ice", as in "Der er is på søen" (There is ice on the lake).

en isenkræmmer.explanation: "En isenkræmmer" means "a hardware dealer". It comes from "isenkram" (hardware, small things for the home). To say where you buy nails and screws, say: "Vi køber søm og skruer hos isenkræmmeren" (We buy nails and screws at the hardware store).

en islænding.explanation: "En islænding" means "an Icelander". It comes from the country "Island" (Iceland). To name the language, use "islandsk" (Icelandic): "Hun taler islandsk" (She speaks Icelandic). Do not mix it up with "en irlænder" (an Irishman): "En irlænder kommer fra Irland" (An Irishman comes from Ireland).
